mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same month predicts a contractionary demand shock, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months signals a late-cycle labor market overheating, which historically precedes equity market corrections. This predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% while the unemployment rate is below 5% signals a supply-side shock in a tight labor market, which historically precedes negative equity returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 70% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 200,000 when the unemployment rate is above 5% signals a recovery from recession, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered recoveries.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for four consecutive months, accompanied by a federal funds rate below 4%, signals a delayed monetary policy response to inflation, which historically precedes positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days as markets anticipate future rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3.0% for four consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 4.0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) of more than 5% while personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) are flat or declining signals a precautionary savings regime, which historically precedes negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days as consumers delay discretionary spending.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 5% AND GDPC1 monthly change <= 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for six consecutive months, regardless of labor market conditions, predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to persistent supply chain weakness.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods.
